title: Split RV32M division across the existing EX/MEM register
motivation: The baseline's 199.837 ns worst path crosses operand forwarding and the EX ALU on its way to data memory. A single-cycle radix-4 prototype reached 5.233 MHz. Splitting the same arithmetic across EX and MEM reached 10.901, 10.542 and 10.542 MHz across the three Gowin placements, versus a baseline median of 5.442 MHz. The split prototype passed the CoreMark CRC checks in the baseline's 4,491,485 bracketed cycles. Its median timing gives 23.47 iterations/s versus 12.12. The reported LUT4 count fell from 12,312 to 4,450.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
For DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU, compute nine radix-4 quotient digits from the forwarded operand magnitudes in EX. Register the 18-bit quotient prefix, 18-bit partial remainder, low 14 dividend bits, divisor magnitude D, 34-bit 3D and sign flags in EX/MEM. Compute the final seven digits in MEM and capture the selected, sign-corrected result in MEM/WB. Two independent divides can issue on successive cycles. An immediate consumer of a nonzero destination uses the existing one-bubble load-use interlock and receives the result from MEM/WB. A dmem stall holds the partial state with the rest of EX/MEM.
Each digit consumes two dividend bits and chooses among 0, D, 2D and 3D using parallel trial subtractions. Form multiples at 34-bit precision. Narrow each subtraction to the consumed dividend-prefix width, use its borrow plus the multiple's upper bits to determine fit, and select the difference for the largest fitting multiple. For a zero divisor every quotient digit is 3 and the remainder retains the dividend magnitude. Suppress quotient negation in this case and apply the dividend sign to the remainder. For INT_MIN divided by -1, the magnitude calculation yields quotient 0x80000000 and remainder zero. Route the specified ALTOPS formulas through the same pipeline boundary.

changes.description: Replace the native DIV/REM expressions with the two divider blocks. Connect both in the standalone combinational ALU and use a parameter to elaborate just the prefix in the core's EX divide path.
Form operand magnitudes and full-width divisor multiples. Resolve the first nine digits and emit the partial state. In ALTOPS mode carry the specified operand difference across EX/MEM.
Reconstruct 2D by shifting D, resolve the last seven digits and restore the selected result's sign. In ALTOPS mode XOR the registered difference with the operation's existing constant.
Define the partial divider state and carry it in ex_mem_t. Share the decoded DIV/REM operation predicate across stages.
Capture the divider prefix state alongside instruction metadata under the existing EX/MEM reset and hold enables.
Finish each divide from registered state and select its result into MEM/WB. Preserve the memory interface and the held WB data used by forwarding.

Mark valid DIV/REM producers alongside loads at the hazard unit's late-result input and exclude unfinished divide results from EX/MEM forwarding. Apply the same interlock in real arithmetic and ALTOPS builds.

Include both divider modules in the ALU build. Extend exact-result checks with dividends bracketing multiples of the divisor, high-bit divisors whose 3D exceeds 32 bits, and seeded full-width operand pairs for all four operations.

Include both divider modules in the pipeline build. Check immediate consumers in both source positions, independent back-to-back divides, writes to x0, and a divide held behind a stalled memory request. Check writeback values and consecutive channel-0 retirement orders.

lesson: - 2026-11-19 hyp-20261119-001-r1s0 (regression, +111.39%): Registering the radix-4 DIV/REM result after the first nine digits at EX/MEM shortened the EX path and raised median Fmax from 5.442 to 11.508 MHz, while the one-cycle interlock for immediate consumers added no cycles to CoreMark.

title: Fold DIV and REM into an eight-round execute unit
motivation:
Gowin reports a 199.837 ns, 156-cell path through operand forwarding and the EX
ALU. The ALU evaluates full-width signed and unsigned division and remainder
combinationally. These are the strongest candidates for that depth. A reference
interpreter run of the canonical 2K binary counted 2,922,015 instructions
between the marker stores, including 93,960 MULs and zero divides or remainders.
Folding only division should therefore shorten the clock period without adding
execution stalls inside the measured interval.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Share one registered restoring divider across DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU. Capture
forwarded operands on issue, then generate four quotient bits per clock for
eight clocks. Four compare/subtract steps between registers replace the full
32-step combinational dependency. Transfer the sign-corrected result into
EX/MEM on the eighth round. All other instructions use the existing EX latency.
At the baseline 4,491,485 cycles for ten iterations, 5.70 MHz would clear the
acceptance threshold at equal cycles, and 8.17 MHz would deliver a 50% gain.
Check median Gowin Fmax and marker cycles together because time spent in
setup can shift the pseudo-random bus stalls seen during measurement.

changes.description:
Replace the four combinational divide/remainder arms with a clocked engine
using unsigned magnitudes, a partial remainder, and a quotient shift register.
Use the subtract borrow to select each restored remainder and quotient bit.
Sign the quotient from both operands and the remainder from the dividend.
Handle divisor zero and INT_MIN divided by -1 explicitly for both result
types. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS capture the existing op-specific substitute
at issue and return it through the same eight-round handshake.

Start once on a valid divide when the older MEM operation can advance.
Latch both forwarded source values for RVFI at issue. While waiting, send
bubbles with cleared controls into EX/MEM so older instructions drain.
On the last round write one normal EX/MEM entry with the result, original
metadata and captured sources. Release ID/EX on that edge so an immediate
consumer can use EX/MEM forwarding. Reset cancels a pending divide.

Hold the fetch PC and ID/EX for a pending divide, including its launch
cycle. Give an older stalled data request priority. Drive the existing
EX/MEM freeze and MEM/WB hold only from data-memory backpressure.

Connect the EX divide-wait signal to hazard control. Route completed
results through the existing in-order writeback and channel-0 retirement.

Clock the divider and sample its result on completion with a bounded wait.
Keep all existing expected results and exercise all four operations on
full-width operands, exact divisions, signed extremes and back-to-back issues.

Exercise an older stalled load feeding a divide, consecutive dependent
divides, and a store consuming the last result under bus stalls. Check
forwarded RVFI operands, the stored value and exactly one retirement per
instruction in order. A taken branch over a divide must skip its issue.

title: Predict direct branches with a synchronous block RAM indexed by the next fetch PC
motivation:
Fetch always selects PC+4. Since IF/ID is combinational, each taken
branch or jump resolved in EX discards one younger fetch opportunity.
Between the CoreMark markers the reference ISS executes 294,425 taken
conditional branches and 49,367 JALs. A scratch RTL prototype of the
predictor below completed the same ten iterations in 4,188,685 bracketed
cycles versus 4,491,485 at baseline, with both stall generators enabled
and all five CRCs matching. Gowin reported 5.218, 5.320 and 5.320 MHz.
The median gives 12.70 iterations/s, 4.79% above the 12.12 champion.
The prototype used one additional BSRAM and 157 additional logic cells.
It passed all 53 single-retirement ALTOPS formal checks and a directed
test of a loop-exit misprediction with imem stalled as dmem resumed.
At this cycle count, clearing the 4.6% threshold requires more than
5.3102 MHz, so placement remains the main uncertainty.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
On an accepted fetch, predict legal conditional branches from the high
bit of a 1,024-entry table of two-bit saturating counters. Drive the
synchronous block-RAM read address from bits [11:2] of the same
next PC that the fetch register samples. This delivers the matching
counter during fetch without adding a pipeline stage. Predict JAL
taken. Compute the direct target once from the current PC and B or J
immediate. Select it only when predicted taken, word-aligned and in
the 1 MiB instruction RAM. Otherwise select PC+4, including for JALR.
Carry both the decision and the computed target into EX. A direction
mismatch on a valid advancing instruction triggers a correction to
the architectural successor. A hit lets the younger instruction enter
ID/EX immediately. Train from the registered outcome in EX/MEM.

changes.description:
Predecode legal BRANCH funct3 and JAL from raw imem_data. For those
instructions, add the signed B/J offset to the current PC. Use one
next-PC mux with priority reset, EX correction, stall hold, then
prediction. Drive imem_addr from the registered PC. Read the 1024x2
simple dual-port block RAM at each rising edge using the selected
next PC. Register a same-index write bypass so a simultaneous update
supplies a defined counter. Initialize the table weakly not taken at
configuration and retain history on core reset. Saturate the sampled
counter toward the registered branch outcome on each training write.

Add direct_target to IF/ID, predicted_taken to IF/ID and ID/EX,
and the sampled two-bit counter to IF/ID, ID/EX and EX/MEM.

For legal B and JAL instructions, put the full computed target in
the existing ID/EX immediate field. Latch the decision and counter
with their instruction under the same hold and bubble controls.

Use the latched absolute target for B and JAL, and the forwarded
rs1 plus immediate with bit zero cleared for JALR. Compare the
resolved aligned transfer decision with predicted_taken. Redirect
only on a valid advancing mismatch, to the same successor reported
in RVFI pc_next. Preserve the misalignment trap and PC+4 link.
Carry the counter snapshot alongside the registered branch outcome.

Write the table once for each valid legal conditional branch in
EX/MEM using its PC, outcome and counter snapshot. Inhibit training
on reset. Feed the EX correction to the existing hazard and IF
redirect inputs. A dmem hold defers correction until EX advances,
when correction takes priority over imem wait or load-use hold.

Train a loop branch taken, then make it fall through with a store
at its predicted target. Hold an older memory operation in MEM as
the exit resolves and deassert imemReady on release. Check that
the fall-through retires once, the branch reports its resolved
successor, and only the architecturally executed stores reach dmem.
